name: John Graunt
summary: Seventeenth-century London haberdasher and pioneer of demographic statistics known for analyzing the Bills of Mortality.

name: Margaret Pelling
summary: Historian at the University of Oxford specializing in the history of medicine and demography.

name: William Petty
summary: English economist, scientist, and philosopher known for political arithmetic and association with Graunt.

name: Royal Society
summary: Learned society for science founded in London in 1660.

name: Sir Robert Moray
summary: Scottish soldier, statesman, and natural philosopher who was the first president of the Royal Society.

name: London Bills of Mortality
summary: Weekly records of deaths and causes of death in London used for demographic analysis.

name: Natural and Political Observations... upon the Bills of Mortality
summary: John Graunt's 1662 pioneering work on demographic statistics and population analysis.

name: New River Company
summary: Company responsible for supplying water to London, of which Graunt was a member.

name: London
summary: Capital city of England where Graunt lived and worked.

name: Bernardino Ochino
summary: Sixteenth-century Italian reformer whose dialogue on polygamy influenced debates Graunt engaged with.

name: Thomas Cranmer
summary: Leader of the English Reformation and Archbishop of Canterbury who invited Ochino to England.

name: Thomas Pecke
summary: Translator of Ochino's dialogue on polygamy into English in 1657.

name: Francis Osborne
summary: English essayist and friend of Pecke whose work praised polygamy.

name: John Heydon
summary: Royalist astrologer and alchemist who replied to Pecke and Osborne on polygamy.

name: Sir Thomas Browne
summary: English author and physician who assumed an excess of women and referenced Ochino.

name: Gregory King
summary: Later political arithmetician whose calculations followed Graunt's.

name: C. H. Hull
summary: Editor of Petty's economic writings and Graunt's Observations.

name: Anthony Wood
summary: Antiquary who described Graunt as 'puritanically bred'.

name: Samuel Pepys
summary: Naval administrator and diarist impressed by Graunt's collection.

name: Richard Smyth
summary: Lawyer who remembered Graunt as an understanding man of quick wit.

name: John Robartes
summary: Member of the privy council to whom Graunt dedicated part of his Observations.

name: Paracelsus
summary: Sixteenth-century physician and alchemist whose text on sex ratios may have influenced Graunt.

name: A defence of Christian liberty to the Lords table
summary: Work from 1646 ascribed to Graunt but not definitively his.

name: A dialogue of polygamy
summary: Notorious dialogue by Ochino published in 1563 and translated in 1657.

name: Advice to a son
summary: Work by Francis Osborne published in 1654/5 and 1658 praising polygamy.

name: Advice to a daughter
summary: Work by John Heydon published in 1659 replying to Osborne and Pecke.

name: The ladies champion
summary: Work by Heydon published in 1660 promoting himself and discussing women.

name: Religio medici
summary: Work by Thomas Browne published in 1643 discussing polygamy and sex ratios.

name: The Historical Journal
summary: Academic journal publishing Pelling's article in 2016.

name: Cambridge University Press
summary: Publisher of The Historical Journal.

name: Wellcome Unit for the History of Medicine
summary: Research unit at Oxford where Pelling was based.

name: University of Oxford
summary: University where Pelling worked and where a conference version was heard.

name: Exeter
summary: Location of the 2008 conference on gender and health.
